prompt: A shop runs on virtual machines rented as IaaS. A critical fix for the operating system is published. Who installs it?
hint: Lesson 1. Where does the line sit in IaaS?

choices.text: The provider, since it runs the hypervisor
choices.why: The hypervisor is the provider's; the guest OS above it is not.

choices.text: The shop's own team
choices.why: Right. In IaaS the operating system and everything above it are the customer's.

choices.text: Nobody: a cloud image patches itself at every boot
choices.why: An image is a template; it holds whatever was in it when it was made.

choices.text: The provider, but only in the premium support plan
choices.why: Support answers questions; it does not take over your operating system.

prompt: Which of NIST's five characteristics is "the provider measures what you used and bills you for it"?

choices.text: Resource pooling
choices.why: Pooling is many customers sharing one set of hardware.

choices.text: Rapid elasticity
choices.why: Elasticity is growing and shrinking; it says nothing about the bill.

choices.text: Measured service
choices.why: Right. Metering is what makes pay-per-use possible.

choices.text: Broad network access
choices.why: That one is about reaching the service over the network from ordinary devices.

prompt: A company moves its e-mail to a SaaS product. What is still the company's job?
hint: Lesson 1. The line is highest in SaaS, and it still has something under you.

choices.text: Patching the mail server's operating system
choices.why: That is the provider's in SaaS; you never see that machine.

choices.text: Nothing: SaaS hands every task to the vendor
choices.why: The data and who may reach it stay yours in every model.

choices.text: Sizing the servers for next year's growth
choices.why: Capacity is the vendor's problem in SaaS.

choices.text: Managing accounts, access and sharing
choices.why: Right. Users, access and configuration remain the customer's.

prompt: Which of these are among NIST's essential characteristics of cloud computing? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: On-demand self-service
choices.why: Yes: you get it yourself, without a person approving.

choices.text: Rapid elasticity
choices.why: Yes: capacity grows and shrinks quickly.

choices.text: One physical server per customer
choices.why: The opposite: resources are pooled among customers.

choices.text: Measured service
choices.why: Yes: usage is metered.

choices.text: A contract of at least one year
choices.why: Nothing in the definition asks for a term.

prompt: Match each model to what is left to you.

pairs.right: The operating system and everything above it

prompt: A team moves its API from virtual machines to a PaaS. Which task leaves its week?
hint: Lesson 1. Which layer did the line just cross?

choices.text: Fixing bugs in the API's own code
choices.why: The code is the customer's in PaaS as well.

choices.text: Upgrading the runtime and the OS below it
choices.why: Right. In PaaS the platform owns the runtime and the operating system.

choices.text: Deciding who may read the customer data
choices.why: Access to data is yours in every model.

choices.text: Rotating the API keys it gave its partners
choices.why: Those keys are part of the application, which is still the team's.

prompt: "The cloud is just somebody else's computer." What does the sentence leave out?
hint: Lesson 1. Think of what a rented server in a datacentre lacks.

choices.text: That the computer is usually faster
choices.why: Speed is not what defines cloud.

choices.text: That the hardware becomes yours after a year
choices.why: Nothing is transferred; you rent use.

choices.text: Self-service by API in minutes, pooled, elastic and metered
choices.why: Right. Those characteristics are what a rented server does not give you.

choices.text: Nothing: the sentence is the NIST definition
choices.why: NIST defines it by five characteristics, not by ownership.

prompt: The line between what the provider runs and what the customer runs is called the shared ___ model.
hint: Lesson 1. Who answers for which layer.

prompt: Functions as a service (FaaS) sit closest to which point on the line?
hint: Lesson 1. What do you hand over?

choices.text: PaaS, with the unit shrunk to one function
choices.why: Right. You hand over code and the platform runs it.

choices.text: IaaS, because a server still runs it somewhere
choices.why: A server exists in every model; the question is who manages it.

choices.text: SaaS, because you buy a finished product
choices.why: In FaaS the application is yours.

choices.text: Outside the line: it is a fourth kind of cloud
choices.why: It is a point on the same line, not a new category.

prompt: Which of these stays the customer's job in IaaS, PaaS AND SaaS alike?
hint: Lesson 1. Two things never cross the line.

choices.text: Choosing the operating system version
choices.why: In PaaS and SaaS the provider chooses it.

choices.text: Replacing a failed disk
choices.why: Hardware is the provider's in all three.

choices.text: Scaling the application servers
choices.why: In SaaS that is the vendor's.

choices.text: Deciding who reaches the data
choices.why: Right. Data and identity are yours whatever you rent.

prompt: What turns a company's virtualised datacentre into a private cloud?

choices.text: Having more than a hundred virtual machines
choices.why: Size does not make it a cloud.

choices.text: The five characteristics, offered to its own users
choices.why: Right. Without them it is virtualisation, not a cloud.

choices.text: Moving the racks to a building the company rents by the year
choices.why: Where it sits does not change what it offers.

choices.text: Buying the hypervisor licence
choices.why: A hypervisor gives virtual machines, not self-service.

prompt: Which of these is a hybrid cloud?

choices.text: Two teams, each on a different public provider
choices.why: That is multi-cloud, and the workloads do not span both.

choices.text: A public cloud used from an office network
choices.why: Every public cloud is reached from somewhere.

choices.text: An app in a public region using a database kept on premises
choices.why: Right. One workload spans both, joined by a link.

choices.text: Servers that are half virtual and half physical
choices.why: That is a datacentre, not a deployment model.

prompt: In one month, 12,000 GB leave sa-east-1 for the internet. The sheet prices the first 10,240 GB at 0.1500 and the next tier at 0.1380 USD per GB. What is the charge?
hint: Lesson 2. The tiers apply one after the other.

prompt: How does the price list treat data going into a region from the internet, compared with data leaving it?
hint: Lesson 2. Read both lines of the transfer block.

choices.text: In is free; out is billed per GB
choices.why: Right. That asymmetry is why leaving a provider costs more than arriving.

choices.text: Both are billed at the same price per GB
choices.why: The sheet shows 0.0000 for data coming in.

choices.text: Out is free; in is billed per GB
choices.why: It is the other way round.

choices.text: Neither is billed inside the free tier, which has no end
choices.why: Egress has a price in every tier of the sheet.

prompt: Which is the WEAKEST reason for running on two public providers at once?

choices.text: A service only one of them offers
choices.why: A real reason: you go where the service is.

choices.text: A customer who requires the other provider
choices.why: A real reason, if the contract is worth it.

choices.text: Resilience, with no plan to fail over
choices.why: Right. Two of everything, and nothing moves when one fails.

choices.text: Negotiating a better discount with each
choices.why: Weak on its own, but not the weakest here.

prompt: A Brazilian company stores customers' personal data in a region in the United States. What does the LGPD say about it?

choices.text: Forbidden: personal data must stay in Brazil
choices.why: The law regulates transfer abroad; it does not ban it.

choices.text: A transfer abroad, allowed in the cases the law lists
choices.why: Right. Article 33 lists when a transfer abroad is allowed.

choices.text: Nothing: the LGPD covers only data on paper
choices.why: It covers personal data in any medium.

choices.text: Nothing, as long as the provider is American
choices.why: The provider's nationality is not the test.

prompt: Which workload is the best candidate for moving out of a public cloud and back onto owned hardware?
hint: Lesson 2. What does elasticity buy, and who does not need it?

choices.text: A shop whose traffic triples every Black Friday
choices.why: Spiky load is where renting shines.

choices.text: A prototype that may be thrown away next month
choices.why: Buying hardware for it would be the mistake.

choices.text: A batch job that runs twice a year
choices.why: Owned hardware would sit idle for months.

choices.text: A service with steady load for years
choices.why: Right. Steady load is where owned hardware can beat rent.

prompt: The more data sits in one place, the more applications move towards it. This pull is called data ___.
What is a community cloud?

choices.text: A public cloud with a free tier
choices.why: A free tier is a price, not a deployment model.

choices.text: An open-source cloud anybody can install
choices.why: Open source describes the software, not who shares it.

choices.text: One shared by bodies with common needs
choices.why: Right. For example, government bodies sharing requirements.

choices.text: A private cloud lent to a neighbour
choices.why: Lending capacity does not make a model.

prompt: In a public cloud, what keeps one customer's machines apart from another's on the same hardware?

choices.text: Each customer gets a separate building
choices.why: Then it would not be pooled.

choices.text: Virtualisation and the provider's software
choices.why: Right. Isolation is done in software on shared hardware.

choices.text: Nothing: tenants can see each other's disks
choices.why: Isolation is exactly what the provider sells.

choices.text: A contract clause that forbids looking
choices.why: A contract does not separate memory.

prompt: Match each virtual machine product to its provider.
What do you need to read AWS's whole price list?
hint: Lesson 3. The course read it without an account.

choices.text: An AWS account and an access key
choices.why: The list is public; no credentials are asked for.

choices.text: A support plan
choices.why: Nothing is paid to read it.

choices.text: Just an HTTP client; it is public JSON
choices.why: Right. curl and jq were enough.

choices.text: A request to a salesperson for a written quote
choices.why: List prices are published; a quote is for discounts.

prompt: On the sheet, m7i.large costs 0.16065 USD an hour in sa-east-1 and 0.10080 in us-east-1. How many percent more is São Paulo? Round to a whole number.
A company already signs its staff in with Microsoft's directory and runs SQL Server. Which provider starts with an advantage there?

choices.text: Hetzner
choices.why: Good machines, but nothing tied to that directory.

choices.text: Google Cloud
choices.why: It can federate, but the advantage is elsewhere.

choices.text: DigitalOcean
choices.why: A developer cloud with no Microsoft stack of its own.

choices.text: Azure
choices.why: Right. Entra ID and the Microsoft licences are home ground.

prompt: What is distinctive about a VPC on Google Cloud, compared with AWS?

choices.text: It is global, with regional subnets inside it
choices.why: Right. On AWS a VPC belongs to one region.

choices.text: It has no subnets at all
choices.why: It has subnets; they are regional.

choices.text: It can only use public addresses
choices.why: Private ranges are the normal case there too.

choices.text: It must be created per zone
choices.why: The opposite: it spans regions.

prompt: What does a smaller provider such as Hetzner or DigitalOcean trade away for a simpler bill?

choices.text: Virtual machines: they only rent physical servers
choices.why: Both rent virtual machines.

choices.text: Breadth: far fewer managed services and regions
choices.why: Right. A few products, done simply.

choices.text: Reliability: their machines are for testing only
choices.why: The toy picture is the wrong one.

choices.text: Security: nothing there is isolated
choices.why: They isolate tenants as the others do.

prompt: Which of these are object storage services? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Amazon S3
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Amazon EBS
choices.why: EBS is block storage.

choices.text: Azure Blob Storage
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Google Cloud Storage
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Google Persistent Disk
choices.why: A block device for a VM.

prompt: Two providers list the same size of machine. The price list alone cannot tell you which bill will be lower. Why?
hint: Lesson 3. What else is on a bill?

choices.text: Because list prices are secret until you sign
choices.why: They are published.

choices.text: Because machines of the same size never differ
choices.why: That would make the comparison easy, not impossible.

choices.text: Transfer, disks and discounts are on other lines
choices.why: Right. The machine is one line of many.

choices.text: Because only the larger provider publishes prices
choices.why: Both publish; the course captured one of them.

prompt: Linode, the virtual machine provider, was bought in 2022 by the edge company ___.

hint: Lesson 3. Look for a region in São Paulo.

choices.text: Azure, through Brazil South

choices.text: Hetzner

choices.text: Google Cloud, with southamerica-east1

prompt: On a typical instance, what is one vCPU?

choices.text: One physical core

choices.text: One hardware thread of a core
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: A share of time on any core, decided at random
choices.why: It is a thread, not a lottery.

prompt: m7i.large costs 0.16065 USD an hour on demand in sa-east-1. What does it cost for a month of 730 hours?
m7i.large in sa-east-1: 0.16065 on demand, 0.09956 on a 1-year reservation with no upfront. What is the discount, in percent, to the nearest whole number?
What does the g in m7g.large say about the machine?

choices.text: Its processor is AWS's Arm chip, Graviton

choices.text: It has a GPU

choices.text: It is the general-purpose family

choices.text: Its memory is measured in gigabits

prompt: An instance keeps a file on an instance store disk, and is stopped and started again. Where is the file?
hint: Lesson 4. Which disk survives a stop?

choices.text: Where it was: stopping keeps every disk
choices.why: Only network volumes survive a stop.

choices.text: Gone, with the host it lived on
choices.why: Right. A restart can land on another host.

choices.text: In a snapshot the provider took automatically
choices.why: Nobody took one unless you did.

choices.text: Moved to the root volume by the hypervisor
choices.why: Nothing copies it.

prompt: Put what happens in order when load rises on an autoscaling group with a target tracking policy.
hint: Lesson 4. It follows the load; it does not predict it.
items: The average CPU goes above the target
The policy raises the desired count
An instance is launched from the template
It boots and passes its health check
It starts receiving traffic
trap: Traffic before the health check is the slip: an instance that is still booting would get requests it cannot answer.

prompt: A web app keeps each user's session in the memory of the instance that served the login. The group scales in overnight. What do some users see?
hint: Lesson 4. What died with the instance?

choices.text: Nothing: sessions move to another instance on shutdown
choices.why: Nothing moves memory between instances.

choices.text: A slower page while the group rebalances
choices.why: Slower is not the problem; gone is.

choices.text: They are signed out: the session died with it
choices.why: Right. State belongs outside the instance.

choices.text: An error until the group scales out again
choices.why: The other instances answer; they just do not know the user.

prompt: Which work suits spot instances?
hint: Lesson 4. They can be taken back.

choices.text: The only database server of a shop
choices.why: An interruption would take the shop down.

choices.text: A restartable batch of video conversions
choices.why: Right. Interruptible, restartable work.

choices.text: A login server that must answer every second
choices.why: It cannot afford a two-minute notice.

choices.text: Anything, since spot is simply cheaper on demand
choices.why: It is cheaper because it can be taken away.

prompt: A file that starts with #cloud-config is read at first boot by the program called ___.

hint: Lesson 4. Time to ready against something else.

choices.text: The image cannot be used by an autoscaling group
choices.why: Groups launch from images all the time.

choices.text: The instance boots more slowly
choices.why: The opposite: less to do at boot.

choices.text: It stops the instance from getting user data
choices.why: Both can be used together.

choices.text: Faster to ready; every change needs a new image
choices.why: Right.

prompt: How do you rename an object in object storage?

choices.text: Copy to the new key, delete the old

choices.text: Edit its first bytes, where the name is kept
choices.why: Objects cannot be edited in place.

choices.text: Move the folder it is in
choices.why: Folders are only prefixes of keys.

prompt: S3 Standard costs 0.04050 USD per GB-month in sa-east-1. What do 500 GB cost for a month?
hint: Lesson 5. One line of the sheet.

prompt: Match each kind of storage to what a program addresses it by.

pairs.right: A path in a shared filesystem
A key in a bucket, over HTTP

right_distractors: A row id in a table

prompt: A block volume is in zone a. An instance in zone b needs it. What happens?
hint: Lesson 5. Where does a volume live?

choices.text: It attaches anyway, only slower
choices.why: Attachment is inside one zone.

choices.text: Both instances can mount it at once
choices.why: Sharing among machines is what file storage is for.

choices.text: It cannot; a snapshot restored in b can
choices.why: Right. Volumes live in one zone; snapshots get you across.

choices.text: The provider moves it the next time it reboots
choices.why: Nothing moves it for you.

prompt: An object store is designed for eleven nines of durability. What does that NOT protect you from?
hint: Lesson 5. Durability is about the bytes surviving the hardware.

choices.text: A person deleting the object by mistake
choices.why: Right. The system keeps what you told it to keep; versioning covers mistakes.

choices.text: A disk failing in the datacentre
choices.why: That is exactly what the copies are for.

choices.text: A whole zone losing power
choices.why: Standard classes keep copies in more than one zone.

choices.text: Bits flipping on a drive
choices.why: Checksums and repair handle that.

prompt: Six web servers behind a load balancer must all serve the images users upload. Where should the uploads go?
hint: Lesson 5. Which storage do many machines share?

choices.text: The local disk of whichever server got the upload

choices.text: One block volume attached to all six
choices.why: A block volume attaches to one instance.

choices.text: A bucket every server reads
choices.why: Right. Shared, cheap per GB, and reached over HTTP.

choices.text: A snapshot taken after each upload
choices.why: A snapshot is a copy of a volume, not a place to serve from.

prompt: What does versioning on a bucket add?

choices.text: Faster reads of the newest version
choices.why: It is about keeping, not speed.

choices.text: A cheaper storage class for old objects

choices.text: Copies in a second region
choices.why: That is replication.

choices.text: Undo for overwrites and deletes

Glacier Instant Retrieval

prompt: How many addresses does a /20 hold?

prompt: On AWS, how many addresses can instances use in a /24 subnet?

choices.text: A route for 0.0.0.0/0 to an internet gateway

choices.text: Addresses outside the RFC 1918 ranges

choices.text: A security group that allows port 80

choices.text: Only for clients inside the VPC

prompt: Match each provider to how it grants access.

pairs.right: Policies attached to identities or resources
Role bindings on a resource, inherited downwards

prompt: Which line in a policy is the first thing to look for in a review?

choices.text: "Version": "2012-10-17" at the top
choices.why: That is the language version and belongs in every policy.

choices.text: "Effect": "Deny"
choices.why: A deny narrows access.

choices.text: "Condition" with an IP range
choices.why: A condition narrows access too.

choices.text: "Action": "*" with "Resource": "*"
choices.why: Right. Everything, on everything.

prompt: What does "serverless" mean?
hint: Lesson 8. The wrong picture is the literal one.

choices.text: The code runs without any server
choices.why: There are servers; you do not see them.

choices.text: Servers you never size or patch
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Code that runs only in the browser
choices.why: Functions run on the provider's side.

choices.text: A virtual machine with no operating system
choices.why: There is one; it is the provider's.

prompt: A function with 512 MB of memory runs 1,000,000 times a month for 200 ms each. How many GB-seconds is that?
hint: Lesson 8. Memory in GB times seconds times calls.

prompt: Lambda charges 0.20 USD per million requests. Ignoring the free tier and compute, what do 3 million requests cost?
Why is the first request after a quiet hour slower on a function platform?

choices.text: The provider throttles accounts that were idle
choices.why: Nothing punishes idleness.

choices.text: The function's code is downloaded from the developer's machine
choices.why: The code is already with the provider.

choices.text: A new environment has to be set up
choices.why: Right. Warm environments are reused; after a quiet spell there may be none.

choices.text: DNS for the function's address expired
choices.why: Name resolution is not the delay here.

prompt: Where does code on Cloudflare Workers run?

choices.text: In a container per function, in one region you choose
choices.why: That describes a regional function platform.

choices.text: In V8 isolates at Cloudflare's locations near users
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: In the visitor's own browser
choices.why: It runs on Cloudflare's machines.

choices.text: On a virtual machine you rent by the hour
choices.why: Nothing is rented by the hour there.

prompt: What do Vercel and Netlify give every pull request of a front-end site?

choices.text: A virtual machine to run the tests on
choices.why: Nothing to manage.

choices.text: A code review by the platform
choices.why: Review is people's work.

choices.text: A separate billing account
choices.why: Billing is per team, not per branch.

choices.text: A preview with its own address
choices.why: Right.

prompt: An API receives a steady, high load all day, every day. Which is likely cheaper, and why?
hint: Lesson 8. Where do the two cost lines cross?

choices.text: Functions, because they scale to zero at night
choices.why: A steady load never reaches zero.

choices.text: Always-on machines, past the break-even volume
choices.why: Right. Per-use pricing loses to a flat rate at high steady volume.

choices.text: Functions, because the free tier covers any volume
choices.why: The free tier is an allowance with a limit.

choices.text: They always cost the same for the same work
choices.why: The pricing models differ; so do the totals.

prompt: What is the longest a single Lambda invocation may run, in minutes?
Put a cold invocation in order.
hint: Lesson 8. Init happens once per environment.
items: A request arrives and no warm environment is free
A new execution environment is created
The code outside the handler runs once
The handler runs for this request
The environment is kept warm for the next one
trap: Running the handler before the init code is the slip: the handler depends on what init prepared.

prompt: Where should a function open its database connection?

choices.text: Inside the handler, on every call
choices.why: A new connection per call wastes time and connections.

choices.text: Outside the handler, reused while warm
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: In the client's browser
choices.why: That would hand the database to anyone.

choices.text: Nowhere; it is not allowed
choices.why: They can; connection counts are the issue.

prompt: What does a region contain?

choices.text: One datacentre
choices.why: A zone may already be more than one.

choices.text: Every edge location
choices.why: Edge locations are not regions.

choices.text: Several isolated availability zones
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: One zone per customer
choices.why: Zones are shared by every customer in the region.

prompt: Light in fibre covers about 200 km per millisecond. What is the minimum round-trip time over a straight 1,000 km path?
A page makes 20 calls one after the other to a server with a 120 ms round trip. What is the least time the calls take together?
hint: Lesson 9. Sequential round trips add up.

choices.text: 120 ms, since they share one connection
choices.why: One connection still pays each round trip.

choices.text: 6 ms each, once the connection is warm
choices.why: Distance does not warm up.

choices.text: 2.4 seconds
choices.why: Right. Twenty times 120 ms.

choices.text: It depends only on the bandwidth
choices.why: Small calls are bound by latency, not bandwidth.

prompt: Two AWS accounts both use sa-east-1a. Are they in the same zone?

choices.text: Yes: zone names are global
choices.why: Names are mapped per account.

choices.text: Not necessarily: compare the zone IDs
choices.why: Right. The ID is the stable name.

choices.text: No: each account gets a private zone
choices.why: Zones are shared; only the names are shuffled.

choices.text: Only if they share a VPC
choices.why: A VPC does not rename zones.

prompt: The recovery point objective says how much ___ you can afford to lose, measured in time.
Order these disaster recovery strategies from the cheapest to run to the most expensive.
hint: Lesson 9. Cost rises as recovery time falls.
items: Backup and restore
Pilot light
Warm standby
Active-active
trap: Pilot light and warm standby are the pair people swap: a pilot light keeps only the core running, warm standby a scaled-down copy of everything.

choices.text: A cache and small code near users

choices.text: A smaller region with one zone

choices.text: The outer zone of a region

choices.text: Where the provider keeps backups

prompt: An application runs in two zones of one region, behind a load balancer. What does that design survive?

choices.text: One zone failing

choices.text: A bad deploy that breaks the code

choices.text: Someone deleting the database

choices.text: The two numbers are a typo in the list

choices.text: Leaving São Paulo costs 7 times more
Data can move only from São Paulo northwards
choices.why: Both directions are allowed and priced.
